record.tranche_reason: The study compares model scales and training-token counts using downstream benchmark performance, rather than testing the original claims with held-out pretraining cross-entropy or a compute-optimal allocation sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream task scores across PaLM sizes and training lengths, including task-specific discontinuities and checkpoint variation. It does not report a parameter/token/compute power-law fit to held-out pretraining loss, predictions of larger-run loss from smaller runs, or compute-optimal parameter/token splits. Kaplan-style scaling is discussed as context; cited results are not study rows.
record.test_reason: PaLM trains 8B, 62B and 540B models identically (except batch size) and reports downstream few-shot performance across those sizes and across training tokens, so it tests V6 directly. It reports no held-out pretraining loss fits, extrapolation or compute-optimal sweeps, so V1, V2, V3, V5 and V7 are untested. A single qualitative parallel-layer ablation bears weakly on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the conclusion section does not mention non-monotonic continued-training results; those come from Appendix F. The authors conclude that few-shot gains from scale have not plateaued and are typically log-linear from 8B to 540B. On a number of benchmarks the gains are discontinuous, suggesting capabilities emerge at sufficient scale. Reasoning breakthroughs come from scale combined with chain-of-thought prompting. They state they did not ablate parameters vs tokens and leave the compute-optimal trade-off and architecture choices as open questions.
record.recipe_differences: PaLM is a three-size dense decoder-only Transformer sweep, evaluated mainly on few-shot downstream tasks; it does not reproduce the original held-out-loss fitting procedure or run a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Task choice changes the apparent scaling pattern: the BIG-bench aggregate is described as log-linear while roughly 25% of tasks have discontinuity greater than +10%; Web Questions varies across checkpoints; and some continued-training benchmark results are non-monotonic. A parallel-layer ablation has a small quality degradation at 8B and none at 62B.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-data memorization rate rises log-linearly with model size (slope 0.002, R²=0.976), 1.6% at 8B to 2.4% at 540B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization of training data scales log-linearly with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Continuing 62B training on repeated subcorpora gives smaller downstream gains than on refreshed data over the same 95B extra tokens (Table 33).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated data is worth less than unique data for downstream performance at large scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Toxicity of continuations rises from 8B to 62B, then plateaus at 540B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Toxicity propensity does not scale monotonically with model size.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant scaling results. Several results are qualitative or figure-only; the paper does not measure held-out pretraining loss for these scale comparisons, and its architecture ablation does not specify a loss metric.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many additional per-task downstream scores, including English NLP, BIG-bench, code, translation, multilingual generation, and bias benchmarks. They are not itemized here because the record prioritizes aggregate results and the explicit task-level departures relevant to predictability; the main tables and figures are in Sections 6.1–6.8, Appendix F, and Appendix H.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is reported against parameters, tokens or compute.
No loss extrapolation from small runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep. Section 13 explicitly says params-vs-tokens ablations were not run.
Depth, width or aspect ratio at fixed parameter count, measured by loss over a wide range.
No power-law fits in other modalities or regimes. The repeated-data and fine-tuning comparisons use downstream scores, not loss laws.
Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss, and any fitted predictive law (only three sizes).
No fitted exponents, no parameter-counting or fitting-method comparison, no compute-optimal estimates.

missing.what: Downstream aggregate vs total training FLOPs. PaLM 8B/62B/540B give an interpolated curve. Chinchilla moderately beats it on BIG-bench and slightly underperforms on 9 English NLP tasks; Gopher falls well below. PaLM 62B at 1.325T tokens matches the English NLP curve but stays below it on BIG-bench.
missing.locator: Section 13, Figure 24, Table 21; Appendix F, Figure 26, Table 31

missing.what: Non-monotonic per-task scaling in the 8B/62B/540B table, e.g. Web Questions 0-shot 62B 11.5 vs 540B 10.6, and COPA 1-shot 62B 93.0 vs 540B 91.0.
Tasks with flat scaling (navigate, mathematical induction): 540B only modestly beats 62B.

record.verdict_notes: V7 links were removed from all rows. Downstream-task discontinuities bear on V6 predictability, not on fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal splits. R21's 'challenges' verdict was dropped: the checkpoint spacing is not a scale manipulation. Only three model sizes exist, so 'log-linear' is a descriptive judgement, not a fit. Continued-training rows confound tokens with a changed data mixture.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling of held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute is reported.
The paper does not fit loss curves on smaller runs and predict loss for substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep seeks a loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
The paper reports a parallel-versus-serialized-layer ablation at 8B and 62B, but does not test a broad range of depth, width, or architecture changes using held-out pretraining loss.
The paper evaluates code, multilingual tasks, and fine-tuned models, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds for loss in those regimes or in other modalities such as images or video.

The study tests downstream performance against model size and training tokens, not downstream performance against pretraining loss; it does not establish a general predictive mapping from pretraining loss to task performance.
The study reports task-dependent discontinuities and some non-monotonic results, but does not compare fitting methods, parameter-counting conventions, or compute-optimal allocation estimates.

statements.correction: Logical-sequence normalized accuracy: 8B 13%, 62B 25%, 540B 87%; smaller-scale projection approximately 37%; deviation +50 percentage points.
